references.text: Earlier, Luke tells us that Jesus was approaching Jericho ([ref:Luk 18:35|Luke 18:35]), where he healed a blind man. Luke 19:1 continues the journey as Jesus enters and passes through the city of Jericho.

Jericho is one of the oldest cities in the Bible. In [ref:Jos 6:1-2|Joshua 6:1-2], Joshua takes the city by God's command. Now Jesus enters that same historic city with a different kind of mission—to seek and save what was lost.

The purpose of Jesus passing through Jericho becomes clear in [ref:Luk 19:10|Luke 19:10]: "For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost." Jesus' entry into Jericho was intentional—he came to find Zacchaeus.

Mark also recounts events connected with Jericho ([ref:Mark 10:46|Mark 10:46]), where Jesus leaves the city after healing blind Bartimaeus. Together with Luke's account, this paints a picture of Jesus' activity in and around Jericho on his way to Jerusalem.

In [ref:Matt 20:29|Matthew 20:29], it is also mentioned that Jesus left Jericho with a large crowd. The parallel passage shows that Jesus' visit to Jericho was part of the final journey up to Jerusalem.

Jericho is also known from the parable of the good Samaritan ([ref:Luk 10:30|Luke 10:30]), where the road from Jerusalem down to Jericho is the place where the man was attacked. Now Jesus himself walks through this city and shows mercy in practice.
This is a clear parallel describing the same travel activity (going through cities and teaching) on the way to Jerusalem, even though it does not specify Jericho.
This is a parallel to Jesus' entry into a city (Jerusalem), sharing the theme with the entry into Jericho, but referring to a later and different event.
This is a parallel describing Jesus' journey toward Jerusalem, although it specifies the region between Samaria and Galilee instead of Jericho.
This is a parallel to Jesus' entry into a city (Jerusalem), sharing the same structure of entering, looking around, and moving on.
This is a direct continuation of the same event; Luke 19:41 describes Jesus' reaction just after he entered the city (Jerusalem) in 19:1 (or within the context of the journey toward Jerusalem).
